Violation Details
Regulation Code

8-201.11
Remodeling or opening prior to having an approved plan review or pre-operational inspection.
RECOMMENDED RESOLUTION: A permit applicant or permit holder shall submit to the regulatory authorityproperly prepared plans and specifications for review and approval.
OBSERVATIONS & CORRECTIVE ACTIONS: At time of inspection, a bbq grill and smoker was observed outside. Discussed that this was not in the original plans that was approved. Discussed the need for a handwashing sink. This is a repeat violation. The owner has been asked multiple times to turn in a plan review application. At time of inspection, a paper copy of the plan review application was provided. The establishment owner must turn in a plan review application for review within 10 days to GCCHD to reflect the changes in the establishment.
3-501.17
Ready-to-eat time/temperature control for safety food improperly date marked.
RISK FACTOR/INTERVENTION
RECOMMENDED RESOLUTION: Ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. The day or date marked by the food establishment may not exceed a manufacturer's use-by date.
OBSERVATIONS & CORRECTIVE ACTIONS: Observed multiple ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods throughout the establishment with no datemarking. Items were housemade bbq, white bbq sauce, ox tail, etc. Discussed the above recommended resolution. Discussed with owner that when transferring a product into a new container that the new container must also be datemarked with the day that the product was made. The establishment must date mark all ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods not used within 24 hours. Email photo verification to inspector within 10 days.
6-301.11
Hand cleaning soap not available at each handwashing sink.
Corrected On Site
RECOMMENDED RESOLUTION: Each handwashing sink or group of 2 adjacent handwashing sinks shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.
OBSERVATIONS & CORRECTIVE ACTIONS: At time of inspection, there was no hand cleaning soap at the kitchen handwashing sink. Owner restocked the sink with soap at time of inspection. This will be marked as corrected on site.
4-302.12
Food temperature measuring devices not readily available.
RECOMMENDED RESOLUTION: Food temperature measuring devices shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of food temperatures. A temperature measuring device with a suitable small- diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin foods such as meat patties and fish filets.
OBSERVATIONS & CORRECTIVE ACTIONS: At time of inspection, the owner was not able to show a thermometer within the establishment. Discussed that the establishment must have a temperature measuring device with a suitable small-diameter probe to measure cooking, cooling, reheating, cold holding, and hot holding temperatures. The establishment must email photo verification of the thermometer within 10 days to inspector.
3-304.12
Utensil stored where there is potential contamination.
Corrected On Site
RECOMMENDED RESOLUTION: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food preparation and dispensing utensils shall be stored In food that is not time/temperature control for safety food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, such as bins of sugar, flour, or cinnamon; or in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, if used with moist food such as ice cream or mashed potatoes.
OBSERVATIONS & CORRECTIVE ACTIONS: Observed multiple in-use utensils stored in one container with room temperature water. Owner removed the utensils from the container at time of inspection. This will be marked as corrected on site.
3-501.15
Inappropriate cooling methods used.
RISK FACTOR/INTERVENTIONCorrected On Site
RECOMMENDED RESOLUTION: Cooling shall be accomplished in accordance with the time and temperature criteria by using one or more of the following methods based on the type of food being cooled: placing the food in shallow pans; separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; using rapid cooling equipment; stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; using containers that facilitate heat transfer; adding ice as an ingredient; other effective methods. Containers must be arranged to facilitate maximum heat transfer and be loosely covered or uncovered if protected from overhead contamination.
OBSERVATIONS & CORRECTIVE ACTIONS: Observed a covered container of potato salad that was in the cooling process. Discussed the above recommendation resolutions. The lid was moved to partially cover the container so that heat can escape at time of inspection. This will be marked as corrected on site.
6-202.14
Toilet room not enclosed or provided with a tight-fitting, self-closing door.
RECOMMENDED RESOLUTION: Except where a toilet room is located outside a food establishment and does not open directly into the food establishment such as a toilet room that is provided by the management of a shopping mall, a toilet room located on the premises shall be completely enclosed and provided with a tight- fitting and self-closing door.
OBSERVATIONS & CORRECTIVE ACTIONS: Observed the toilet room door open at time of inspection. It is not a self-closing door. The area right outside of the door is clean equipment and dish storage. Additionally, there was a temporary food event vendor working in the area immediately outside of the toilet room. Owner closed the door at time of inspection. Discussed the above recommended resolution. The establishment must install a tight-fitting and self-closing door within 30 days and email photo verification to inspector.
6-501.12
Physical facilities not maintained cleaned.
RECOMMENDED RESOLUTION: Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of food is exposed such as after closing.
OBSERVATIONS & CORRECTIVE ACTIONS: Observed multiple surfaces that had a build-up of debris such as handles to coolers. Observed build-up of dust on walls and ceilings. Both handwashing sinks had a build-up of debris in the sink and on the handles. The establishment is in need of a deep clean. Email photo verification to inspector within 30 days.
4-501.11
Equipment not maintained in good repair or condition.
RECOMMENDED RESOLUTION: Equipment shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements.
OBSERVATIONS & CORRECTIVE ACTIONS: At time of inspection, observed the front panel of the ice machine to be coming off. Additionally observed that the ice machine is draining into a bucket. Owner indicated that the pump is currently not working to drain the condensation out of the bucket. There was no air gap at time of inspection. Owner removed the bucket so that it drained into a different container with an air gap. Discussed that this is not a permanent solution and the pump must be fixed so that the ice machine drains properly. At time of inspection, the storage room freezer was not working. However, items were still frozen and an IR temp of 30F was measured. Owner is aware and said that the electrician has been contacted. Discussed ensuring that time/temperature control for safety foods do not go above 41F. The establishment must fix the pump within 14 days and email photo verification of pump and proper air gap to inspector. The establishment must have the freezer fixed within 14 days. Establishment cannot use the freezer if the temperature goes above 41F. Email written verification to inspector that the freezer has been repaired and properly working.
4-901.11
Utensils not adequately air dried or cloth dried.
RECOMMENDED RESOLUTION: After cleaning and sanitizing, equipment and utensils: shall be air-dried or used after adequate draining before contact with food; and may not be cloth dried except that utensils that have been air-dried may be polished with cloths that are maintained clean and dry.
OBSERVATIONS & CORRECTIVE ACTIONS: Observed staff drying dishware with a cloth towel. Discussed that dishes cannot be cloth dried and must be air dried. Discussed the above recommended resolution at time of inspection with owner. The establishment must email written verification to inspector that dishware are going to be air dried within 14 days.
